subject: Science (GCSE Biology, Chemistry, Physics)
source: Seeded from gcse-science/y10 lesson 107 (V = IR practice sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 107: Voltage, resistance and V = IR. To understand the relationship between voltage, current and resistance

model.title: A 12 V supply drives current through a 4 Ω resistor. Find the current.

questions.q: A lamp has 2 A through it and resistance 6 Ω. Voltage? [2 marks]
questions.model: Formula: V = I × R. Substitute: 2 × 6. Calculate: 12. Unit: V.

questions.q: Current through a 50 Ω resistor on 230 V?
Using the table, what happens to current when resistance doubles?
Core: Eight V = IR questions (portal worksheet), including mA conversions.
questions.a: Answers in the key, e.g. 250 mA through 40 Ω: 10 V.
questions.model: Teacher does question 1: 0.5 A through 20 Ω: V = 0.5 × 20 = 10 V.

questions.q: Extend: Explain how turning a dimmer up makes a lamp brighter. [3 marks]
questions.a: Resistance of the variable resistor decreases (1); total resistance falls so current increases (1); more energy transferred to the lamp per second (1).

questions.q: Stretch: A resistor has 3 V across it and 60 C pass through it in 2 minutes. Find its resistance.
I = V ÷ R. 6 V, 3 Ω gives...
Big question: how does a dimmer switch change a lamp's brightness?
questions.a: It changes the resistance: more resistance means less current and a dimmer lamp.
